captures.description: THE CONTROL PLANE READ WHOLE, §13'S TABLE EXACT, THE LIMITS KEPT: asked for the arguments of Baseline Capture Architecture (v2.0, the submitted state), grounded in the text, ChatGPT says it read the deposited v2.0 (Alexanarch ×9) and quotes §1 ('The data needed to measure the selector's errors may itself be destroyed by the selector.'); the four channels C0–C3 and the replay bank; content-independent inclusion relative to a fidelity locus; Npq and e^−Npq; Horvitz–Thompson against Hájek; correlated misses; the retention map; CMS Zero Bias, Level-1 Data Scouting and the Global Trigger test crate as components, not an implementation; §13's four regimes — 1.000 throughout, 0.759 against 0.016, 0 in [0, 0.073], 0.021 in [0, 0.064], 5,371 against 7,925 stored, the rare class at Npq 0.16 — and §14's limits.

atoms.evidence: The argument of Lee Sharks’s Baseline Capture Architecture
Baseline Capture Architecture for Learned Scientific Triggers (EA-SEI-BCA-01 v2.0)
the paper is a proposal for selection metrology: making the omissions of an irreversible learned selection system measurable after the fact.
The text carefully distinguishes the classical Horvitz–Thompson estimator
Sharks proposes a separate measurement architecture—a Baseline Capture Architecture (BCA)—to make those failures measurable without replacing the trigger or requiring it to stop selecting events.
He explicitly does not claim that these systems already implement BCA.
The text carefully distinguishes the classical Horvitz–Thompson estimator, which is unbiased for population totals under the stated sampling conditions, from the Hájek ratio estimator
The v2.0 record identifies §13 as the principal addition over the earlier v1.0 deposit
